*Written for version 0.1.13. Full instructions: [SKILL.md](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/r-analysis-workflow/blob/main/plugin/skills/initialize-analysis/SKILL.md).*

## What it is for

Setting up a new analysis project, or tidying an existing one (a folder of scripts, or one long R Markdown file), so it becomes a GitHub repository in a consistent layout that the next person can pick up.

## When to use it

- You have an idea, a protocol or an old script, and no repository yet.
- You have a repository that grew without a plan and want it organized.
- A setup was started in an earlier chat and not finished.

## What happens

The assistant asks a short set of questions, one at a time, and reuses anything you have already told it or that is already in the files. It does not ask you to install R or Git unless the work needs them; a clinician can help with the protocol from the browser.

Then it proposes a setup plan and, once you agree, drafts:

- **the analysis plan** (`analysis-plan.md`), from a template that fits the design (observational, economic or descriptive), with a **decision issue** for every scientific choice still open rather than a guess;
- **AGENTS.md**, the project's rules for any assistant: who the deciders are and for what, every data source and the package that reads it, and what an assistant may never read;
- **the website starter**, a README, a reference list, and a `.gitignore` that keeps data and secrets out of the repository;
- **steps for the maintainer** to protect the main copy, so every change arrives through a pull request, and to switch on the website.

It also offers, without requiring them: your own ChatGPT or Claude project for this repository with instructions filled in for how you like to work, milestones with dates, and a periodic check-in that tells you what is waiting on you.

## What it will not do

- Choose a scientific option. It drafts the options; a decider settles them.
- Open data that may be restricted while taking stock of a folder.
- Install tools, publish anything or change repository settings on its own.

## Ask it, for example

- "Set up my R analysis project from my latest RMD and protocol."
- "I have no GitHub account and no R. Help me get this project started."
- "We started setting this up last week; carry on from where it stopped."
